oneOf.description: The first frame of every connection: the extension's version and the API versions it speaks.
A method call; `id` is chosen by the extension and echoed in the answer.
Cancels a running call (`search.start`); the call ends with `error {code: "cancelled"}`.

AnnouncedLimits.description:
Every limit of the API, as `welcome.limits` announces them: the values this companion enforces (the defaults
are in `docs/api.md`).

binarySniffBytes.description: Bytes sniffed for a NUL to call a file binary.

commitTimeoutMs.description:
Longest a commit with its hooks (and `devtab doctor --commit`) may take, in milliseconds: then git and
everything it started are stopped (`hook-timeout`).

diskFloorBytes.description: Least free space on the volume of the companion's state or of the project (`disk-low` below it).

editSessionMs.description:
A file's editing session ends after this many milliseconds without a write to it; a new session starts with
a new "before" copy.

maxBrowserConnections.description: Most browser connections open at once, for the whole supervisor.

maxChangedPaths.description: Most paths in one `files.changed` event (`more` above it).

maxFolderFiles.description: Most files in a folder that is renamed or deleted (`too-many-files` above it).

maxFrameBytes.description: Largest frame the supervisor sends; longer messages are cut into `chunk` frames.

maxGitPaths.description: Most paths one `git.commit` or `git.rollback` names (`invalid-params` above it).

maxHistoryPage.description: Most points on one page of `history.project`.

maxHookOutputBytes.description: Most bytes of a hook's output in an error's `data.output` (the end is kept, the cut marked).

maxHookStreamBytes.description: Most bytes of git's and the hooks' output streamed by one `git.commit` (the rest is not streamed).

maxRequestBytes.description: Largest request frame from the extension, in bytes (`invalid-params` above it).

maxSearchBytes.description: Most bytes streamed by one `search.start` (`truncated` above it).

maxSearchMatches.description: Most matches of one `search.start` (`truncated` above it).

maxTextBytes.description: Largest text of a file, a diff side or a history point, in bytes (`too-large` above it).

maxTreeEntries.description: Most entries of one `tree.list` answer (`truncated` above it).

minSaveIntervalMs.description: Least time between two `file.save` of one file, in milliseconds (`rate-limited` sooner).

readsPerSecond.description: Read calls per second, for the whole supervisor (`rate-limited` above it).

relayMaxInBytes.description: Largest frame Chrome sends to a native host.

relayMaxOutBytes.description: Largest frame Chrome accepts from a native host; the relay refuses to forward more.

searchesPerConnection.description: Searches running at once on one connection.

snapshotBudgetBytes.description: Most bytes of the companion's "before" copies, for all projects together (`disk-low` once reached).

writesPerSecond.description: Write calls per second, for the whole supervisor (`rate-limited` above it).

ErrorCode.description: Every error code of API version 1.

oneOf.description: The request does not match the method's schema: an unknown field, a wrong type, a frame above the limit.
The method is not one this companion knows or offers; `welcome.methods` lists those it offers.
The path breaks the path rules: absolute, `.`/`..`/empty segments, `\`, NUL or control characters, too long.
No such project, file or history point.
After canonicalisation the path lies outside the project root (a symlink leading out).

The path is in a protected place: any segment that folds to `.git` is never read, shown or written (`rule`: `git-dir`); a write through a symlink or to one (`symlink`) and a write to a file that is read-only on disk (`read-only-file`) are refused; `git.rollback` does not bring back a file whose restoring would run a filter of the repository (`git-filter`), a submodule (`submodule`) or a symlink (`symlink`).
A write to a secret file (secrets are readable, never written from the browser): saving, creating, renaming, deleting, restoring from history.
A method that needs a writable ("mine") project, called in a view project.
A write while writing is paused.
The file is binary: not read, not edited.
The text is above `limits.maxTextBytes`.
A folder with too many files for the operation (`limits.maxFolderFiles`).
The file changed since `baseHash`; nothing was written. `currentHash` is the version on disk now.
Create or rename over an existing file or folder.
HEAD or files on disk changed since the page showed them (`git.commit`, `git.rollback`); nothing was done. `paths` names the files that changed (empty when HEAD moved): read the status again.
Hunks were chosen of a file that can only be committed whole (`reason` as `git.hunks.reason`, `new-file` included, or `does-not-apply`); nothing was committed.
A commit with nothing checked, or whose checked files hold no change against HEAD.
git has no `user.name` / `user.email` for the repository; checked before any hook runs. git's own text (with a guessed address) is not passed on.
A hook stopped the commit; nothing was committed. `hook` is the hook that most likely failed, `exitCode` git's exit code, `output` the end of the output (at most `limits.maxHookOutputBytes`).

A hook could not find a program ("command not found", "No such file or directory"); nothing was committed. `pathCapturedAt` is when the environment's `PATH` was captured (null: never, the default `PATH` was used).
The commit ran out of time (`limits.commitTimeoutMs`): git and everything it started were stopped, no lock file of it is left; nothing was committed.
A lock file of the repository (`.git/index.lock`, a ref's lock) belongs to another git; nothing was done.
Signing the commit failed (the signing program of the person's git configuration); nothing was committed.
The last commit cannot be undone: `reason` is `moved` (HEAD is not the commit shown), `pushed` (a remote branch has it), `merge`, `root` (the first commit) or `detached` (no branch).
A merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert is in progress in the repository (`operation`): finish it in a terminal; nothing was committed.
The remote branch has new commits (not a fast-forward).
The remote refused the push.
No credentials for the remote.
git or ssh wanted to ask something in a terminal.
No remote can be chosen.
HEAD is detached.
The push ran out of time.
The network is unreachable.
The person declined in the companion's window, or did not answer within 120 seconds.

The companion cannot show its window (`reason`: `no-window` — no window in this version or no graphical session; `requests-off` — after three declines in ten minutes, until `devtab resume-requests`). `command` is what the person can run in a terminal instead.
Another confirmation is already waiting.
Too many calls; retry after the given time.
The server is restarting; retry after the given time.
No API version in common (`hello`).
The call was cancelled by a `cancel` frame.
The Trash is unavailable; nothing was deleted. This version has no Trash yet, so `file.delete` always answers this and is not listed in `welcome.methods`.
A commit or push waits for the companion's window.
Free disk space is below the floor, or the companion's "before" copies reached their budget; nothing was written.
The text has characters the file's encoding cannot hold, or (`history.restore`) a copy that is not UTF-8 would go into a file that is not `windows-1252`; nothing was written.
The relay could not reach the supervisor; sent by the relay just before it exits.
The connection's peer is not allowed: a wrong origin at the relay, a process other than the relay on the browser socket, a sandboxed process, another user. Sent just before the connection closes.
The supervisor already has as many browser connections as it allows.
Anything else; details go to the supervisor's debug log only.

server.description: A frame from the supervisor (or, for `error` with code `not-running` / `peer-not-allowed`, from the relay).

oneOf.description: The answer to `hello`.

api.description: The API version chosen: the highest both sides speak.

limits.description: Every limit, with the value this companion enforces.

methods.description: The methods this companion offers; the extension hides what is missing.

server.description: The version of the pinned server the companion runs.

oneOf.description: The result of a call.
A failed call; `id` is null when the error is not about a call (handshake, connection).
One part of a streaming method's answer; a `result` with the same `id` ends the stream.
An event about a project the connection subscribed to, or about the companion (`project` null).

One piece of a message longer than the frame limit: the message as a JSON string, cut at character
boundaries; join `data` by `seq` until `last` and parse the joined string as a frame.
